title: Information Security Policy
text:
Information Security Policy

Brightwater Logistics · version 1.1

Purpose: This document describes how Brightwater Logistics protects its information and systems.

1. Governance
Responsibilities for information security are assigned to named roles, led by the CISO. Security topics are only discussed with management when an incident occurs. The company has registered with the responsible authority and keeps an up-to-date contact list for reporting. Exceptions must be documented and approved. Every project passes a security checkpoint before go-live. Legal requirements relevant to information security are tracked in a register maintained by the legal department. This policy was approved by the executive board and is published on the intranet for all employees. Due to the small team, administrators approve and implement their own changes.

2. Risk management
Residual risks above the risk appetite are formally accepted by the board. Questions about this document can be addressed to the information security team. The risk register is updated whenever new risks are identified. The risk management standard defines how threats, vulnerabilities and impact are assessed.

3. People
Annual security awareness training is mandatory for all staff. Candidates for sensitive positions undergo background checks before hiring. Contractors are not bound by confidentiality agreements. Leavers are reminded of their ongoing confidentiality obligations in the exit interview. Violations of security policies are handled in a defined disciplinary process.

title: Access Management Procedure
text:
Access Management Procedure

Kestrel Health Services · version 3.8

Purpose: This document describes how Kestrel Health Services protects its information and systems.

1. Access control
Workstations lock automatically after 10 minutes of inactivity. Service accounts are inventoried and their passwords are rotated regularly. An annual recertification of user permissions is carried out by the line managers. Exceptions must be documented and approved. Administrators use separate privileged accounts that are not used for email or browsing. MFA with an authenticator app is mandatory for VPN and privileged accounts. Emergency access is possible via a shared administrator password without logging. Several teams still share one login for the warehouse system.

title: Secure Development Guideline
text:
Secure Development Guideline

Quillon Software · version 4.9

Purpose: This document describes how Quillon Software protects its information and systems.

1. Secure development
Test environments use synthetic or anonymised data only. Pull requests require at least one approving review. The build pipeline includes SAST and DAST scans that block critical findings. Secrets are stored in a vault; secret scanning prevents them from being committed. Dependency scanning alerts the team about vulnerable open-source components. Developers follow secure coding guidelines based on the OWASP Top 10. Software is developed according to a secure development lifecycle with security activities in every phase.

2. Vulnerability management
Software and systems without vendor support are identified and replaced on schedule. Patches are installed irregularly, sometimes months after release. Independent testers carry out an annual penetration test. A published security contact and disclosure policy allow researchers to report vulnerabilities. Found vulnerabilities are tracked in tickets until they are fixed and verified. Questions about this document can be addressed to the information security team.

title: Network Security Concept
text:
Network Security Concept

Harbourline Shipping · version 1.8

Purpose: This document describes how Harbourline Shipping protects its information and systems.

1. Network security
Exceptions must be documented and approved. Remote desktop is reachable directly from the internet. Firewall rules are reviewed every six months and unused rules are removed. A DDoS protection service filters traffic to the web shop. DNS filtering prevents access to malicious domains. The network is divided into segments for office, production and administration.

2. Cryptography
Certificates are renewed automatically 30 days before they expire. Keys are generated, stored, rotated and destroyed according to the key management standard. Developers choose encryption algorithms on their own.

title: Operations Handbook (security excerpt)
text:
Operations Handbook (security excerpt)

Ostara Foods · version 2.6

Purpose: This document describes how Ostara Foods protects its information and systems.

1. Operations
Every user can install any software on their laptop. Questions about this document can be addressed to the information security team. Changes are made directly in production without a formal process. Secure configuration baselines are defined and checked automatically. Operating procedures for all critical systems are documented in the operations handbook. Security alerts are only reviewed during business hours. All endpoints run an endpoint detection and response agent that is centrally managed. Development, test and production run in separate environments with separate access. Storage, CPU and network capacity are monitored and forecast quarterly. Security-relevant events from servers, firewalls and applications are collected in a central SIEM. Time synchronisation via NTP ensures consistent timestamps across systems. Security logs are retained for twelve months. Integrity of the log archive is protected by hashing and restricted access.

title: Physical Security Standard
text:
Physical Security Standard

Pellucid Payments · version 3.9

Purpose: This document describes how Pellucid Payments protects its information and systems.

1. Physical security
The building is protected by a fenced perimeter and badge-controlled doors. The server room has fire detection, a gas extinguishing system and an uninterruptible power supply. Visitors sign in at reception and are accompanied by an employee at all times. Every entry to the data centre is recorded and reviewed monthly. The requirements apply to all locations and subsidiaries. Confidential printouts are regularly left on desks overnight.

2. Asset management
Owners are assigned to every application and data set. Compliance with this document is checked during internal audits. All servers, laptops and business applications are listed in a maintained asset inventory. Information is not classified according to its protection need. An acceptable use policy defines how company devices and accounts may be used. Email and document templates apply the classification label automatically.

title: Internal Audit Report: ISMS
text:
Internal Audit Report: ISMS

Tamsin Hospitals · version 4.8

Purpose: This document describes how Tamsin Hospitals protects its information and systems.

1. Governance
A compliance register lists all legal and contractual security obligations, including NIS2. Exceptions must be documented and approved. Responsibilities for information security are assigned to named roles, led by the CISO. This policy was approved by the executive board and is published on the intranet for all employees. Contact details of the national CSIRT and the supervisory authority are maintained in the crisis handbook. Key security metrics are reported to management in a monthly dashboard. Requesting, approving and implementing a change are performed by different people. Project charters include a security assessment that the CISO signs off.

2. Risk management
A full information security risk assessment is carried out every year. Risk treatment measures are tracked with responsible owners and target dates. Risks are assessed using a documented methodology that rates likelihood and impact on a five-point scale. The risk register is updated whenever new risks are identified. Risk owners from senior management sign the acceptance of remaining risks. The requirements apply to all locations and subsidiaries.

3. Asset management
Each asset in the inventory has a named owner. Leavers return laptops, phones and access badges on their last working day, documented in a checklist. There is no complete overview of the IT systems in use. Information is classified as public, internal, confidential or strictly confidential. Employees acknowledge the rules for acceptable use of IT resources when they join. Email and document templates apply the classification label automatically.

4. Access control
HR triggers the deactivation of all accounts on the last working day. Access is granted on a need-to-know basis and limited to the minimum required. Remote access and all administrator logins require multi-factor authentication. The password policy requires long passphrases and blocks commonly used passwords. Sessions in business applications end after 15 minutes without activity. Group logins have been replaced by personal accounts for all staff. Joiner and mover requests require documented approval before accounts are created or changed. Administrators use separate privileged accounts that are not used for email or browsing. Service accounts are inventoried and their passwords are rotated regularly.

title: NIS2 Readiness Assessment
text:
NIS2 Readiness Assessment

Verdant Rail · version 2.6

Purpose: This document describes how Verdant Rail protects its information and systems.

1. Incident management
Significant incidents are reported to the national authority with an early warning within 24 hours. Affected systems are reinstalled immediately without securing evidence. An incident response plan defines roles, escalation paths and communication. This document applies to all employees, contractors and temporary staff. After every major incident, a post-incident review documents lessons learned. Security incidents are reported to the CISO within one hour of detection. Incident response procedures are tested annually in a simulated attack.

2. Suppliers
Cloud services are only used after a security assessment, including data location and certifications. Supplier access is granted only for the duration of the assignment and is monitored. Critical suppliers are reviewed annually against their security obligations. The requirements apply to all locations and subsidiaries.

3. Business continuity
Emergency and recovery plans exist for all critical business processes. The continuity plan has never been exercised. Recovery time objectives were derived from a business impact analysis. Questions about this document can be addressed to the information security team. An immutable, offline copy of all backups protects against ransomware. A full restore test of the ERP system is performed twice a year.

4. Cryptography
Certificates have expired unnoticed several times in the past year. Keys are generated, stored, rotated and destroyed according to the key management standard. Exceptions must be documented and approved. Databases and backups with personal data are encrypted at rest. Data is only transmitted over encrypted channels; outdated protocols are disabled.

title: IT Security Concept
text:
IT Security Concept

Lumen Telecom · version 4.6

Purpose: This document describes how Lumen Telecom protects its information and systems.

1. Operations
Administrators can modify or delete the logs of their own systems. Operating procedures for all critical systems are documented in the operations handbook. Servers are configured according to hardening baselines based on CIS benchmarks. Security logs are retained for twelve months. A change advisory board approves all significant changes before implementation. Malware protection is missing on several servers. Production is isolated from test systems; developers have no write access to production. A security operations centre monitors alerts 24/7. Log data of all critical systems is forwarded to a central log management platform. Users cannot install software; installations are made through the software centre.

2. Vulnerability management
Critical patches are installed within 7 days of release. Found vulnerabilities are tracked in tickets until they are fixed and verified. No penetration test has been performed so far. All internal and external systems are scanned for vulnerabilities weekly. Reports of vulnerabilities from external parties are handled through a defined process. Software and systems without vendor support are identified and replaced on schedule.

3. Network security
A semi-annual firewall rule review is documented by the network team. Internet-facing services are protected by the provider's DDoS mitigation. The network plan is updated with every change to the infrastructure. Internet traffic is not filtered. The network is divided into segments for office, production and administration. Remote access to internal systems is only possible through the company VPN. The corporate Wi-Fi uses WPA3-Enterprise; guests use a separate network.

title: Information Security Policy
text:
Information Security Policy

Northcove Insurance · version 2.0

Purpose: This document describes how Northcove Insurance protects its information and systems.

1. Governance
The CISO reviews this document every twelve months; the last review was completed in March. Compliance with this document is checked during internal audits. Responsibilities for information security are assigned to named roles, led by the CISO. The CISO presents a security status report to the board every quarter. Project charters include a security assessment that the CISO signs off. The company has registered with the responsible authority and keeps an up-to-date contact list for reporting. A company-wide information security policy has been drafted but not yet approved by management.

2. Risk management
All information security risks are recorded in a central risk register. The security team subscribes to threat intelligence feeds and evaluates relevant warnings weekly. The risk management standard defines how threats, vulnerabilities and impact are assessed. Risk owners from senior management sign the acceptance of remaining risks. A full information security risk assessment is carried out every year.

3. People
Confidentiality obligations remain in force after the end of employment. Phishing simulations are run every quarter, followed by targeted training. Annual security awareness training is mandatory for all staff. References and certificates of good conduct are checked before employment starts. Violations of security rules have no consequences.

Critical patches are installed within 7 days of release. Reports of vulnerabilities from external parties are handled through a defined process.

Purpose: This document describes how Brightwater Logistics protects its information and systems.

1. Governance
A Chief Information Security Officer is appointed and reports directly to the managing director. The company has registered with the responsible authority and keeps an up-to-date contact list for reporting. Due to the small team, administrators approve and implement their own changes. This document applies to all employees, contractors and temporary staff. Projects are planned and delivered without a defined security review. All security policies are reviewed annually and after major organisational changes. This policy was approved by the executive board and is published on the intranet for all employees. Key security metrics are reported to management in a monthly dashboard.

2. Risk management
The requirements apply to all locations and subsidiaries. It is unclear who may accept residual risks. A full information security risk assessment is carried out every year. Risks are assessed using a documented methodology that rates likelihood and impact on a five-point scale. Each identified risk has a treatment plan with an owner and a due date. The security team subscribes to threat intelligence feeds and evaluates relevant warnings weekly. All information security risks are recorded in a central risk register.

3. Asset management
Owners are assigned to every application and data set. Information is not classified according to its protection need. An inventory of all hardware, software and information assets is kept in the CMDB. Questions about this document can be addressed to the information security team. Email and document templates apply the classification label automatically.

4. Access control
The password policy requires long passphrases and blocks commonly used passwords. Workstations lock automatically after 10 minutes of inactivity. Group logins have been replaced by personal accounts for all staff. Administrators use separate privileged accounts that are not used for email or browsing. Access rights have never been reviewed after they were granted. Access is granted on request without a defined policy. All technical service accounts are listed with an owner and purpose. Accounts of leavers are disabled within 24 hours of their departure. Joiner and mover requests require documented approval before accounts are created or changed. Emergency access is possible via a shared administrator password without logging.

title: NIS2 Readiness Assessment
text:
NIS2 Readiness Assessment

Quillon Software · version 3.0

Purpose: This document describes how Quillon Software protects its information and systems.

1. Incident management
The incident response plan describes how security incidents are detected, contained and resolved. The requirements apply to all locations and subsidiaries. Employees must report suspected security incidents to the service desk immediately, at the latest within one hour. Findings from incidents are tracked as improvement measures. All incidents are handled in the order they come in. The incident response team runs a tabletop exercise twice a year.

2. Suppliers
A security questionnaire and evidence review are mandatory for new IT service providers. Every new cloud service is approved by the CISO before use. Suppliers are not reviewed after onboarding. Supplier contracts do not contain security requirements.

3. Business continuity
Backups are encrypted and stored in a second location, with an offline copy. The business continuity plan is exercised every year, most recently with a data centre failover. All business data is backed up daily. There is no business continuity plan. Restoring from backup has never been tested. Recovery time objectives were derived from a business impact analysis.

4. Cryptography
All certificates are tracked in an inventory with automated expiry alerts. Databases and backups with personal data are encrypted at rest. Only algorithms approved in the cryptography concept may be used. Some internal interfaces still transfer data over unencrypted FTP. Keys are generated, stored, rotated and destroyed according to the key management standard.

title: IT Security Concept
text:
IT Security Concept

Verdant Rail · version 3.5

Purpose: This document describes how Verdant Rail protects its information and systems.

1. Operations
This document applies to all employees, contractors and temporary staff. Time synchronisation via NTP ensures consistent timestamps across systems. Security logs are retained for twelve months. Logs are only stored locally on each system. Changes to production systems require an approved change request. Storage, CPU and network capacity are monitored and forecast quarterly. Secure configuration baselines are defined and checked automatically. All endpoints run an endpoint detection and response agent that is centrally managed. Operating procedures for all critical systems are documented in the operations handbook. Integrity of the log archive is protected by hashing and restricted access.

2. Vulnerability management
A published security contact and disclosure policy allow researchers to report vulnerabilities. Exceptions must be documented and approved. Several servers still run an operating system that no longer receives updates. Critical patches are installed within 7 days of release. Independent testers carry out an annual penetration test. Each finding is assigned an owner and a deadline and followed up until closure. Vulnerability scans are not performed.

3. Network security
DNS filtering prevents access to malicious domains. A current network diagram documents all segments and interfaces. All systems are in one flat network. The requirements apply to all locations and subsidiaries. Guests use the same Wi-Fi as employees. A semi-annual firewall rule review is documented by the network team.
